items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Ram Ramirez had replaced Billy Kyle. When we arrived at the place we were to play... Buster Baily and I found a quiet place and he instructed me on how some of the numbers went.

ctx.x: I renewed my acquaintance with Willy Lewis whom I had met in 1933, in Monte-Carlo with June Cole and Ted Fields. Willy was leading an orchestra in a high society club called "Chez Florence", on rue Blanche and not far from the bar and hotel de Lizieux where many of the American negro musicians would congregate when they had finished their nights work.

But the surprise of surprises was meeting Benny Carter one night at the Lizieux's bar a few nights after I had arrived in Paris. As I had been in Cincinnati a few months before coming to France and the way I was obliged to pass through the Apple, I had not picked up on the latest events, so I had no idea that Benny was in Paris until I saw him this night. He was working with Willy Lewis who had an all-Negro band which was the only one in Europe. Benny had come to Paris with a young pianist named Garnet Clark. I…

Between Boudon's and Lizieux's, that corner was a little Harlem in the early morning when all the night spots were closed and the American musicians and entertainers gathered in those bars and the "tabac".
